fields.title: Represent a zero-row table-valued parameter as a null reference
fields.context: Microsoft.Data.SqlClient validates SqlDbType.Structured parameter values on the client at execution time. Verified with driver 7.0.3 against SQL Server 15.0 on 2026-09-21: DBNull.Value throws NotSupportedException; an IEnumerable<SqlDataRecord> with zero elements throws ArgumentException because no record exists to supply the TDS column metadata; a null reference executes and the server observes an empty table, for both stored-procedure and text commands. SqlParameterCollectionExtensions currently uses DBNull in one overload and an empty list in the other nine, so every empty collection written as a TVP fails client-side. The attribute-driven path (SqlMapAttributes.AppendCollectionInParameterExpressions) assigns TypeName to prms[prms.Count - 1] after the call, so the parameter must always be appended.
fields.decision: Every AddSqlTableValuedParameter overload appends the Structured Input parameter unconditionally and assigns Value = null when the materialized row list is empty or the supplied collection is null. The raw IEnumerable<SqlDataRecord> overload passes null through and normalizes a cheaply-detectable empty collection (ICollection / IReadOnlyCollection with Count == 0) to null without enumerating a lazy sequence. Non-empty behavior is unchanged.

alternatives.option: Keep DBNull.Value for the empty case (current model overload).
alternatives.whyRejected: The driver rejects it with NotSupportedException before any SQL runs; the comment claiming SQL Server treats a DbNull TVP as an empty table describes server-side DEFAULT semantics the client never reaches. Verified empirically.

alternatives.option: Pass the empty List<SqlDataRecord> through (current nine overloads).
alternatives.whyRejected: The driver rejects it with ArgumentException: zero records cannot supply TDS row metadata. The driver's own error text prescribes a null reference instead. Verified empirically.

alternatives.option: Throw ArgumentException from ArgentSea when the collection is empty.
alternatives.whyRejected: An empty collection is a legitimate, common value (a parent with no children). Throwing pushes a Count check onto every caller and gives the attribute-driven path no hook to avoid it.

alternatives.option: Omit the parameter when the collection is empty and rely on the procedure's implicit empty default.
alternatives.whyRejected: Breaks the attribute path, which stamps TypeName onto the last parameter in the collection; also changes the parameter shape between empty and non-empty calls and fails for text commands that reference the parameter.

alternatives.option: Send a single SqlDataRecord with no rows or a metadata-only record.
alternatives.whyRejected: SqlDataRecord is a row; there is no metadata-only record in the SqlClient API. Any record sent is a row the server would insert.

fields.consequences: Empty and null collections execute and produce an empty table server-side. Callers that worked around the failure by skipping the parameter or pre-checking Count can remove the workaround. Tests that asserted DBNull must assert a null reference. The spec corpus must state the rule: behavior blk-48f70a8f347b4bb8aa4490079567c4c9 and schema blk-0539e7af93cc455ba620a90d60dd1467 currently describe only the non-empty shape.
